questions.prompt: Which process removes CO₂ from the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Plants and algae take in CO₂.

questions.prompt: Which organisms can fix nitrogen gas into a form plants can use?
options: Certain bacteria, such as Rhizobium in legume roots
Convert nitrates back into nitrogen gas

questions.prompt: How does burning fossil fuels change the carbon cycle?
options: It removes CO₂ from the air
It releases stored ancient carbon into the air much faster than natural processes remove it

questions.prompt: Too much fertiliser washing into a lake can cause…
options: algal blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish

questions.prompt: Which process links the carbon and oxygen cycles?
questions.explain: CO₂ in, O₂ out, and the reverse.

questions.prompt: Why do farmers sometimes grow peas or beans between cereal crops?
options: Their root nodules add nitrogen to the soil

questions.prompt: Trace one carbon atom from the air, through living things, and back to the air.
questions.modelAnswer: A carbon atom in CO₂ in the air is taken in by a leaf during photosynthesis and becomes part of a glucose molecule. A goat eats the leaf, and the carbon becomes part of the goat’s body. When the goat respires, the carbon is released as CO₂ in its breath, returning to the air (or, if the goat dies, decomposers release it as CO₂).
